opcodes.name: struct.new
opcodes.description: allocates a structure with canonical RTT (runtime type) and initialises its fields with given values

stack.note: One value per field of type x, in declaration order. A packed i8 or i16 field takes an i32.

opcodes.name: struct.new_default
opcodes.description: allocates a structure of type $t with canonical RTT (runtime type) and initialises its fields with default values

stack.note: Every field gets the default value for its type.

opcodes.name: struct.get
opcodes.description: reads field i from a structure

stack.note: t is the type of field y. Only for an unpacked field. A packed i8 or i16 field is read with get_s or get_u, which extend it into an i32. Traps on a null reference.
Field y is packed (i8 or i16), so it is read into an i32 — sign-extended by struct.get_s, zero-extended by struct.get_u. Traps on a null reference.
Field y is packed (i8 or i16), so it is read into an i32 — sign-extended by struct.get_s, zero-extended by struct.get_u. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: struct.set
opcodes.description: writes field i of a structure

stack.note: t is the type of field y, which must be mutable. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: array.new
opcodes.description: allocates an array with canonical RTT (runtime type)

stack.note: t is the element type of x: the value to fill with, then how many elements.

opcodes.name: array.new_default
opcodes.description: allocates an array with canonical RTT (runtime type) and initialises its fields with the default value

stack.note: How many elements; each gets the default value for the element type.

opcodes.name: array.new_fixed
opcodes.description: allocates an array with canonical RTT (runtime type) of fixed size and initialises it from operands

stack.note: One value per element — n of them, given as an immediate rather than taken from the stack.

opcodes.name: array.new_data
opcodes.description: allocates an array with canonical RTT (runtime type) and initialises it from a data segment

stack.note: Offset into data segment y, then how many elements to read from it.

opcodes.name: array.new_elem
opcodes.description: allocates an array with canonical RTT (runtime type) and initialises it from an element segment

stack.note: Offset into element segment y, then how many elements to read from it.

opcodes.name: array.get
opcodes.description: reads an element from an array

stack.note: The array, then the index. t is the element type of x. Only for an unpacked field. A packed i8 or i16 field is read with get_s or get_u, which extend it into an i32. Traps on a null reference.
The element type of x is packed (i8 or i16), so it is read into an i32 — sign-extended by array.get_s, zero-extended by array.get_u. Traps on a null reference.
The element type of x is packed (i8 or i16), so it is read into an i32 — sign-extended by array.get_s, zero-extended by array.get_u. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: array.set
opcodes.description: writes an element to an array

stack.note: Array, index, then the value. The element type must be mutable. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: array.len
opcodes.description: inquires the length of an array

stack.note: Takes any array. Traps on null.
Array, the offset to start at, the value to write, then how many elements. Traps on a null reference.
Destination array and offset, source array and offset, then how many elements. Traps on either being null, or on either range running past the end.
Array, the offset to start at, the offset into data segment y, then how many elements.
Array, the offset to start at, the offset into element segment y, then how many elements.

opcodes.name: ref.test
opcodes.description: checks whether a reference has a given heap type

stack.note: httop is the top of the hierarchy the immediate heap type belongs to — any, func or extern — so the operand may be any reference in that hierarchy. 1 if the reference matches the immediate type, 0 if not. ref.test null counts null as a match.

opcodes.name: ref.test null
opcodes.description: checks whether a reference has a given heap type

stack.note: httop is the top of the hierarchy the immediate heap type belongs to — any, func or extern — so the operand may be any reference in that hierarchy. 1 if the reference matches the immediate type, 0 if not. ref.test null counts null as a match.

opcodes.name: ref.cast
opcodes.description: tries to convert to a given heap type

stack.note: httop is the top of the hierarchy the immediate heap type belongs to — any, func or extern — so the operand may be any reference in that hierarchy. Traps if the reference does not match, and on null.

opcodes.name: ref.cast null
opcodes.description: tries to convert to a given heap type

stack.note: httop is the top of the hierarchy the immediate heap type belongs to — any, func or extern — so the operand may be any reference in that hierarchy. Traps if the reference does not match. Null passes.

opcodes.name: br_on_cast
opcodes.description: branches if a reference has a given heap type

stack.note: rt1 and rt2 are the two immediate heap types, each made nullable or not by a bit of the castflags byte. Branches to l with the reference typed rt2 if it matches; otherwise leaves it on the stack with rt2 subtracted from its type, which is what the backslash means.

opcodes.name: br_on_cast_fail
opcodes.description: branches if a reference does not have a given heap type

stack.note: rt1 and rt2 are the two immediate heap types, each made nullable or not by a bit of the castflags byte. The mirror of br_on_cast: branches when the reference does not match.

opcodes.name: any.convert_extern
opcodes.description: converts an external value into the internal representation

stack.note: Nullability is carried through: a non-null operand gives a non-null result, and null converts to null.

opcodes.name: extern.convert_any
opcodes.description: converts an internal value into the external representation

stack.note: Nullability is carried through: a non-null operand gives a non-null result, and null converts to null.

opcodes.name: ref.i31
opcodes.description: creates an i31ref from a 32 bit value, truncating high bit

stack.note: Only the low 31 bits are kept; the value is not boxed on the heap.

opcodes.name: i31.get_s
opcodes.description: extracts the value, sign-extending

stack.note: Sign-extends the 31-bit value to i32. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: i31.get_u
opcodes.description: extracts the value, zero-extending

stack.note: Zero-extends the 31-bit value to i32. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: ref.i31_shared
opcodes.description: creates a shared i31ref from a 32-bit value, truncating the high bit

stack.note: As ref.i31, but the result may be passed between threads.

opcodes.name: struct.new_desc
opcodes.description:
allocates a struct with an explicit descriptor, taking the descriptor and the field values

The 2022 draft of the GC proposal used this byte for i31.new; that draft was replaced before it was standardised, and the byte is being assigned again.

stack.note: The field values, then the descriptor on top. y is the descriptor type declared for x.

opcodes.name: struct.new_default_desc
opcodes.description:
allocates a struct with an explicit descriptor, its fields set to their defaults

The 2022 draft of the GC proposal used this byte for i31.get_s; that draft was replaced before it was standardised, and the byte is being assigned again.

stack.note: The descriptor. Every field gets the default value for its type.

opcodes.name: ref.get_desc
opcodes.description:
reads the descriptor a reference was allocated with

The 2022 draft of the GC proposal used this byte for i31.get_u; that draft was replaced before it was standardised, and the byte is being assigned again.

stack.note: y is the descriptor type declared for x. Traps on a null reference.

opcodes.name: ref.cast_desc_eq
opcodes.description: casts a reference, checking that its descriptor is the one given rather than checking its type

stack.note: The reference to cast, then the descriptor to compare against. Succeeds where the reference’s own descriptor is that same object. ref.cast_desc_eq null lets null pass; the other traps on it.

opcodes.name: ref.cast_desc_eq null
opcodes.description: casts a reference, checking that its descriptor is the one given rather than checking its type. The nullable form

stack.note: The reference to cast, then the descriptor to compare against. Succeeds where the reference’s own descriptor is that same object. ref.cast_desc_eq null lets null pass; the other traps on it.

opcodes.name: br_on_cast_desc_eq
opcodes.description: branches if a reference’s descriptor is the one given

stack.note: rt1 and rt2 are the two immediate heap types, each made nullable or not by a bit of the castflags byte. As br_on_cast, but matching on descriptor identity rather than on the type alone; br_on_cast_desc_eq_fail branches when it does not match.

opcodes.name: br_on_cast_desc_eq_fail
opcodes.description: branches if a reference’s descriptor is not the one given

stack.note: rt1 and rt2 are the two immediate heap types, each made nullable or not by a bit of the castflags byte. As br_on_cast, but matching on descriptor identity rather than on the type alone; br_on_cast_desc_eq_fail branches when it does not match.
